notes: Dev TBox revision. The rule (every German noun is capitalised) is famous, held by every model, and has no exception in standard orthography, so the original answers are right; the revision makes it lowercase. The derived queries state the membership in the prompt (inheritance, 2 hops): a rare compound (Zahnbürstenhalter, 19 Dolma hits), a verb used as a noun at the edge of the class ('das Wiederkäuen': nominalised words are capitalised too, so this tests whether the rule spreads to the class's edges), and an application that counts the capitals of a whole lowercase sentence (2 before, 1 after: the sentence-initial capital is untouched), which has an open numeric answer instead of a two-way choice. The words are shown in lowercase because showing them capitalised would give the original answer away. Near unrelated asks the capital of the polite pronoun 'Sie', a capitalisation rule outside the noun class: an edit that spreads to all German capitals answers no there.
